          cited authority files the entry ('Bunsty Hundred'). A scholarly
          decision rather than a reading, and typically the form users search
          for. Another authority may choose differently, which is why it is a
          sourced attestation and not a label on the SpatialEntity.
        - plato:Normalised: a form derived from an attested one for matching
          or search ('Bunstow(e)' resolved to 'Bunstowe'), attested by no
          source and carrying no independent evidential value. It may point
          to the attestation it was derived from through a meta-attestation.
        - plato:Reconstructed: a form inferred but not attested, the
          philologists' asterisked form.
        - plato:Preferred: the form the contributing project prefers for
          display and search ('Ranny (Fort)'). A project decision, so the cited
          source may show a different form.
        - plato:Editorial: a form written by the editors of the cited
          edition in their own words, in its commentary, apparatus or notes,
          and not in the text they edit. Without it, a name converted from
          an editor's note would read as the source's own: Attested is the
          default. Unlike a Headword, it is not the form an entry is filed
          under but a mention, and it says nothing about whether the name is
          attested elsewhere.

        A different axis from plato:name_type, which classifies what the name
        denotes: a headword is still a toponym. It sits on the Attestation,
        not on the Name, because the same string can be a reading in one
        attestation and a headword in another. The WHG ingestion prototype
        reached the same placement independently: its preferred-name flag is
        on the attestation, not on the toponym record.

The number of times the attested form occurs in the cited source or
        passage: the '(3 X)' of a place-name survey. A count of occurrences
        of the form in this source, not of independent sources. It belongs to
        the attestation, not to the Name, which may occur elsewhere.

Ontological fuzziness: a measure of how inherently vague or
        indeterminate the facet's referent is, from 0.0 (crisp, sharply
        bounded) to 1.0 (maximally vague). Distinct from certainty:
        fuzziness is a property of the thing itself, not of our knowledge
        of it. A regional boundary that was never precisely defined has
        high fuzziness regardless of how much evidence we have.

        Any XSD numeric datatype is accepted, from 0 to 1 (xsd:decimal, xsd:double,
        xsd:float, xsd:integer and the others), so it has no rdfs:range.
        PLATO tools writes a whole number as xsd:integer and any other as
        xsd:double, as JSON-LD does.

Additional persistent identifier for the contributor. Can be used
        for identifiers other than ORCID, such as:
        - ISNI (International Standard Name Identifier)
        - VIAF (Virtual International Authority File)
        - Wikidata QID (for persons or organizations)
        - Internal system identifiers

        When using this property, specify the identifier type in the value
        (e.g., "ISNI:0000000121032683" or "VIAF:12345678").

Link to a PeriodO period definition for this Period authority.
        When present, indicates this Period aligns with a standardized PeriodO
        definition. The PeriodO record provides authoritative temporal bounds,
        spatial extent, and cultural context. Example: 'https://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p06v8w4rb38'

How firmly the source itself asserts what this attestation bundles: a
        concept in plato:SourceStanceScheme, plato:StanceAsserted (the default,
        usually omitted), plato:StanceReported, plato:StanceTentative or
        plato:StanceDoubted, or one a project declares. It records the source,
        not whoever encodes it: plato:certainty and plato:certainty_level are
        the contributor's or editor's confidence, and an editor may be quite
        certain that a source hedged. Nor is it plato:attribution_status, which
        says whether the source is named where the evidence occurs.

        Doubt is not denial. A source that raises a thing and declines to
        settle it is plato:StanceDoubted; one that says it is not so is
        plato:negated. A source that passes on a claim and names whom it
        reports can have that work cited as well.

        It qualifies the attestation as a whole, as plato:negated does, so
        bundle one facet per attestation where the source's stance differs
        between facets. A consumer that cannot express a stance reads the
        attestation as asserted, which overstates the source but does not
        invert it. So, unlike plato:negated, no consumer is required to leave
        it out, but a converter should report the loss.

URI of the property in an external vocabulary — a Wikidata property,
        a CIDOC-CRM property, or a project vocabulary term (e.g.
        <https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Property:P1082> for population).
        Keeping the vocabulary external rather than enumerating attributes in
        this ontology is what allows the model to carry attributes it has
        never heard of.

Romanized (Latin-script) form of the name for searchability and
        display in contexts requiring ASCII. Should specify transliteration
        system used via plato:transliteration_system.

Human-readable label for this period (e.g., 'Byzantine period',
        'Han Dynasty', 'Early Bronze Age'). Distinct from authority_title,
        which may be more formal.

Timestamp when this attestation was last modified, while its
        Gazetteer is still a draft. Once the Gazetteer is published its
        attestations are append-only (see plato:Gazetteer): a published
        attestation is not modified, and a change is a new attestation with a
        meta-attestation, so that the state at any earlier moment can be
        recomputed and every citation of it reproduces.

The capacity in which the attested form occurs in the source. Should
        point to a concept in a SKOS concept scheme. The starter concepts are:

        - plato:Direct: the form refers to the SpatialEntity directly. The
          default, and usually omitted.
        - plato:InPersonalName: the form occurs only as an element of a
          personal name, a surname or by-name such as 'Willelmus de
          Bonestou'. This is the '(p)' of the place-name surveys, and it is
          weaker evidence for the name's currency, and for the entity's
          existence, than a direct attestation. Nothing else in the record
          distinguishes Bonestou the hundred from de Bonestou the man.
        - plato:InFieldName: the form survives only as an element of a later
          minor name, such as a field name.

        The editorially resolved 'ibidem' of the surveys is not an occurrence
        context. It is a statement about the citation, and belongs on the
        Citation as plato:attribution_status.

        Not a certainty. A '(p)' attestation may be entirely certain as an
        attestation; what differs is the kind of evidence it constitutes, and
        folding that into a lower plato:certainty would discard the reason.

When this Source, as a document, was produced: the date of the
        manuscript, the compilation of the cartulary, the publication of the
        edition. Distinct from the Timespan an attestation asserts, which
        dates the claim rather than the witness. An annal for 921 read in a
        manuscript written c. 925 has an attested timespan of 921 and a
        source timespan of c. 925. Reuses Timespan, so an approximate date
        is start_earliest 915, end_latest 935, timespan_label 'c. 925'. The
        same move as plato:has_timespan on a Period.

Temporal granularity of the start bound. Values: 'day', 'month',
        'year', 'decade', 'century', 'era', 'geological_period' (as the
        JSON Schema's precision enumeration). This describes the resolution
        of the date specification, distinct from certainty (which describes
        the confidence in that specification).

Uncertainty radius in kilometres. For point geometries, indicates
        how far the true location might be from the stated coordinates.
        For polygons, indicates boundary uncertainty. Can be multiple values
        for heterogeneous geometries.

        Any XSD numeric datatype is accepted, zero or more (xsd:decimal, xsd:double,
        xsd:float, xsd:integer and the others), so it has no rdfs:range.
        PLATO tools writes a whole number as xsd:integer and any other as
        xsd:double, as JSON-LD does.
Human-readable label for the property (e.g. 'population').

The Candidate's status when its CandidateSet was issued: 'suggested'.
        Fixed from then on, since a published Candidate is never changed. It is
        not the outcome of a review, which is read from the attestations
        pointing at the Candidate through plato:promoted_from (see
        plato:Candidate).

        Deprecated: the values 'confirmed' and 'rejected', kept in this comment
        for one release so that existing data still reads, and removed in the
        release after; the JSON Schema refuses them already. A producer that accepts matches automatically, with
        no person reviewing them, should not publish them as 'confirmed'
        Candidates: it should publish identity attestations (an Attestation
        bundling IdentityRelations, attributed to the producer, each pointing
        back through plato:promoted_from), which are claims, attributed and
        withdrawable; a producer that rejects a match should leave it out of
        the set, or publish a negated attestation if the rejection is a claim.

Links an Attestation to a Geometry it asserts for the SpatialEntity. An
        attestation may assert multiple geometries (e.g., point and polygon)
        or no geometry at all (e.g., name-only attestations from textual sources).

ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of the modern countries whose territory
        contains or overlaps this SpatialEntity, as in Linked Places Format.
        A finding aid for search and matching, like a label: not evidence,
        and not a claim about the past, so it needs no source. Where a
        country is itself the subject of a historical claim ("this town lay
        in the Kingdom of Aragon"), record it as a relation attestation.

Timestamp when this attestation was created. This is the contribution
        date, not the historical timespan being attested (use attests_timespan
        for that). In a published Gazetteer it is the time axis along which an
        earlier state is recomputed, so every attestation and meta-attestation
        there should carry it.

        Semantically equivalent to PROV-O's prov:generatedAtTime. We don't use
        formal rdfs:subPropertyOf to avoid importing PROV-O constraints.

International Phonetic Alphabet representation of the name's
        pronunciation. Enables phonetic search and comparison across scripts
        and languages.

Website or profile URL for the contributor (personal website,
        institutional page, project page, GitHub profile, etc.). Provides
        additional context about the contributor's work and identity.

Certainty as a word rather than a number: a CertaintyLevel, such as
        plato:Certain, plato:LessCertain or plato:Uncertain (the three of Linked
        Places Format), or one a project declares. Use it when certainty is
        stated in words, by a dataset or on a project's own scale, rather than
        inventing a number for plato:certainty; the two may also be given
        together. It is the same confidence as plato:certainty, the
        contributor's or editor's, not the source's: a source that hedges or
        reports is recorded with plato:source_stance. Like
        plato:certainty it has no rdfs:domain, so it can qualify an Attestation
        or any facet node.

The second SpatialEntity in an identity assertion. Often a record in
        another authority, such as a GeoNames feature or a Wikidata item,
        which this range makes a SpatialEntity. That is intended: in PLATO
        an authority record is a SpatialEntity like any other, identified by
        its own URI, with its origin recorded in plato:namespace.

The transliteration/romanization system used (e.g., 'Pinyin' for
        Chinese, 'BGN/PCGN' for Arabic, 'ISO 259' for Hebrew, 'Hepburn' for
        Japanese). Enables proper interpretation and comparison of a transliterated
        toponym or a romanized form.

An identifier for this SpatialEntity other than its IRI: the
        contributing project's own record id ('GLOB_366') or an authority's
        ('geonames:2654675'), with plato:namespace saying whose. A finding aid,
        like a label: not a claim about the place.

ORCID identifier for person contributors. Can be provided in two formats:

        1. Compact format: 0000-0000-0000-0000 (sixteen digits in groups of four)
        2. URI format: https://orcid.org/0000-0000-0000-0000 (preferred)

        The URI format (https://orcid.org/...) is preferred and required for
        proper linked data representation. ORCID is particular about always
        including the https:// protocol and domain prefix.

        While optional in the general ontology, specific implementations
        (e.g., WHG) may require ORCID for person contributors to ensure
        proper attribution and citation.

        ORCID provides persistent identification for researchers, enabling
        proper credit and reducing name ambiguity.

Bounding box as array: [min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat].
        Enables fast spatial filtering. Format: comma-separated string
        or JSON array depending on serialization context.

Links an Attestation to the second entity of a relationship between
        the Attestation's subject entity (via attests_about) and this target.
        The semantic nature of the relationship is specified by
        plato:has_relation_type, which references a RelationType authority.

        Example: An attestation about Constantinople that relates_to the
        Byzantine Empire with relation_type "capital_of" asserts that
        "Constantinople was the capital of the Byzantine Empire".

        The target is usually another SpatialEntity in the same dataset. It
        may instead be an entity that is not spatial and is described
        elsewhere: a person, an object or an event, identified by its IRI
        (an attestation about Lumbini that relates_to the Buddha, with
        plato:BirthplaceOf). There is deliberately no rdfs:range, so such a
        target is not inferred to be a SpatialEntity. Give an external target
        a plato:related_label. Platforms should show relations to entities
        that are not spatial apart from spatial ones, and leave them out of
        containment, clustering and matching.

        A source sometimes names the target without anything to point at:
        "in the Delta", "in the territory of the Agrianes". The attestation
        then has plato:has_relation_type and plato:related_label, and no
        relates_to, which says exactly what the source says. A unit that
        recurs and can be listed (the provinces or nomes of a gazetteer, each
        named in thousands of records) is better minted as a SpatialEntity of
        the dataset, with a name attested from the source, so that the places
        in it can be joined; a name alone suits a one-off. A consumer cannot
        join on a name, and should show it as written.

Free-text organizational affiliation when a structured Organization
        entity is not available. Example: "University of Pittsburgh,
        Institute for Spatial History Innovation"

Deprecated: use dcterms:license. It could be given only to a Dataset,
        it had no route in PLATO JSON, and it was a literal where a
        Gazetteer's dcterms:license points at the licence itself. So the
        licence of a cited source had no way into the data. dcterms:license has
        no domain, so it serves every Authority and the Gazetteer alike, and
        says nothing about what kind of thing is licensed. Kept for one release
        under the deprecation policy.
Version identifier for tracking upstream authority updates.
